mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust the giver's and receiver's counts before processing any later statements. Subsequent statements refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the problem includes 'X gives K to Y' statements and later statements reference X or Y.
mathgap.example: A later comparison uses X's original count even though an earlier 'X gives K to Y' transfer has already changed X's amount.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form 'the number of onions that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of onions that C and D have' into the signed equation (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the phrase 'the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have.'
mathgap.example: Interpreting the same statement as |A - B| = |C - D| and solving with absolute values.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'Person has N onions', set that person's current count to N at that moment, after any earlier transfers. This count is used for all subsequent references.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever an explicit count is given for a person.
mathgap.example: Later using the person's count as N even though a prior transfer has already altered it.

mathgap.title: Update both parties in a transfer
mathgap.principle: For a statement 'X gives K onions to Y', subtract K from X's current count and add K to Y's current count at that point.
mathgap.example: Only adding K to Y's count while leaving X unchanged.

mathgap.title: Accumulate net change for multiple transfers
mathgap.principle: If a person appears in several transfer statements, sum all gains and losses to compute their net change before using the resulting count in later equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a person is involved in more than one transfer.
mathgap.example: Treating each transfer separately and writing contradictory equations for the same person.

mathgap.title: Systematic linear solving
mathgap.principle: After translating all statements into linear equations, solve the system using substitution or elimination, ensuring each variable satisfies all constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After all constraints have been collected.
mathgap.example: Guessing a value for a variable without solving the equations, leading to inconsistency.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All derived counts must be non‑negative integers; if any equation yields a negative or fractional value, revisit sign conventions or transfer handling.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the system, before final answer.
mathgap.example: Obtaining a negative count for a person because a difference was taken with the wrong sign.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrasing 'difference between the number of X that A and B have' is ambiguous, leading the model to default to absolute value.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate such statements directly to (A - B) = (C - D) preserving order; do not apply absolute value.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes all transfers happen simultaneously, so later statements use pre‑transfer counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process the problem line by line, updating counts after each transfer before evaluating later statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats 'Person has N' as a final state, overlooking that later transfers may modify the count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as the current count at that point in the text; apply any subsequent transfers to update it.

mathgap.description: Updating only the receiver in a transfer
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the gain and forgets the corresponding loss for the giver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When processing 'X gives K to Y', subtract K from X and add K to Y.

mathgap.description: Reversing the direction in 'X has N more than Y' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model misreads the phrase and writes Y = X + N instead of X = Y + N.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'X has N more than Y' as X = Y + N.
